title: Beyond the 956: Irma P. Hall, “Soul Food’s” Big Mama, dies at 91
excerpt: Irma P. Hall, the actress beloved as Big Mama in the 1997 film “Soul Food,” died November 10, 2026, at 91 in Dallas, Texas.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Irma P. Hall, the actress beloved as Big Mama in the 1997 film Soul Food, has died at 91.

Hall died Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Dallas, Texas, where she lived with her family, her family announced in a statement released Wednesday. She was 91. A cause of death was not publicly disclosed, and memorial arrangements will be announced later.

“Irma P. Hall was a beloved actress, author, poet, educator, and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career,” her family said in the statement. “Her legacy of talent, dedication, and compassion will continue to inspire generations to come.”

Born June 3, 1935, in Beaumont, Texas, Hall grew up on Chicago’s South Side and taught school in Texas — at Booker T. Washington High School in Houston and James Madison High School in Dallas — before her acting career took off in her late 30s.

She became a familiar face in film and television over five decades, often playing strong matriarchs. Her turn as Josephine “Big Mama” Joseph, the heart of the family in Soul Food, earned her the NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Motion Picture. In 2004, she starred opposite Tom Hanks in the Coen brothers’ The Ladykillers as Marva Munson, a performance that won her the Jury Prize at the Cannes Film Festival.

Her many other credits included A Family Thing, Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil, Beloved, Collateral, and Patch Adams, and television roles on Soul Food: The Series, Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago Fire, and Hap and Leonard.

Rest in Peace, Irma P. Hall.

Sources: family statement, reported by WFAA (November 11, 2026); Baller Alert (November 11, 2026); Blex Media (November 11, 2026).
